subject: SAFEGATE: simulation plan for private patch window, network gating & rollback
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Acme Ops <acme-ops@acmehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: SAFEGATE: simulation plan for private patch window, network gating & rollback

Hi team,

Following our last runbook rehearsal, I'm proposing a short, instrumented maintenance simulation against the Acme Health private deployment next Thursday (2026-11-19). Goal: validate our version-pin unpin + rollback path under realistic network gating and firewall churn. This is a simulation (no customer-facing change) but will exercise:

- version pinning/unpin flow for private nodes (pin->canary->sweep)
- network gating (ingress-only controls, NVAs, and LB drain behavior)
- KMS rotation interaction during active traffic (read-only checks)
- telemetry & audit trail generation (audit-logs, traces, token-level cost spikes)
- rollback triggers (latency > 200ms p95 OR error rate > 1.5%)

Please review the attached draft maintenance-sim-plan (PDF) and runbook checklist (md). High level ask: confirm you can join the shiproom on Thu 11/19 09:30 PT for a 60-minute drill, and provide any objections by EOD tomorrow.

Initial timeline:
- 09:30 PT: shiproom & blast radius confirmation
- 09:40 PT: create canary (5% traffic) using pinset v2026-11-15-b
- 09:50 PT: apply ingress gating rule to canary subnet (simulate firewall rule flip)
- 10:00 PT: monitor telemetry for 20 minutes; if stable, sweep to 100% else trigger rollback
- 10:30 PT: postmortem & evidence capture

Attachments: maintenance-sim-plan, runbook-checklist.

Notes: Acme Ops — we will need a firewall exception for the simulation (outlined in the attached firewall-change-request). Can you confirm you can implement the gating change in a maintenance sandbox?

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Staff SRE, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Acme Ops <acme-ops@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T12:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SAFEGATE: simulation plan for private patch window, network gating & rollback

Diego — thanks for the clear plan. A few technical bullets from runtime/serving perspective: 

- Canary sizing: 5% is fine if the sequence length distribution is representative. Prefer to pin CPU-bound workers only for the first canary so we avoid global KV cache invalidations.
- Pin mechanics: ensure the pinset carried the model + quant profile. For the simulation, use a non-idempotent pin tag (v2026-11-15-b-sim) so we can audit it without conflicting with production pins.
- Network gating: instead of a full firewall flip, do a two-step NVA policy: (1) route canary egress through NVA-A with observability hooks; (2) flip ingress rule on LB to drop a 1% sample to simulate partial connectivity loss. This gives a smoother failure mode to validate rollback triggers.
- Rollback automation: the script should support both automatic rollback (on threshold breach) and manual confirmation with a single-ack gate in the shiproom. I'll attach a small snippet to the runbook.

Couple of asks:
1) Monica/So, confirm we have isolated telemetry dashboards (token-level and p95/latency) populated for canary before the window.
2) Ops: include the firewall-change ticket ID in the runbook so the audit trail links to their change log.

I'll be on the shiproom.

—Karthik
(technical notes appended in quoted runbook snippet)
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-18T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SAFEGATE: simulation plan for private patch window, network gating & rollback

Diego / Karthik — quick compliance check: 

- Audit evidence: For SOC2 we need immutable evidence that the pin/unpin and firewall change were performed and who approved them. Please ensure the runbook includes (a) change approver (DocuSign ID acceptable) and (b) the firewall-change ticket ID and a copy of the change window.
- KMS keys: If the simulation touches key metadata, run it with read-only key ACLs and capture key-id in telemetry. Don't rotate keys during the sim.
- Data residency: confirm logs are retained in the customer-controlled bucket for 90 days (Acme requirement).

I can provide the compliance checklist to include in the runbook. Also, please CC security@redwood.ai if any deviation is expected.

Rachel
Director of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SAFEGATE: simulation plan for private patch window, network gating & rollback

Thanks — updated plan attached. Quick responses inline: 
- Audit evidence: we'll create an immutable change bundle (runbook snapshot + firewall ticket + DocuSign approval) and upload to the customer evidence Drive folder immediately post-sim. DocuSign link will be added before the shiproom begins.
- KMS: agreed — read-only access and no rotation until after postmortem. We'll log key-id: projects/redwood/keys/acme-prod-readonly in telemetry.
- Logs retention: confirmed with Monica; logs retained to Acme's S3 path for 90 days.

Shiproom invite sent for 2026-11-19 09:30 PT. Canary tag: v2026-11-15-b-sim.

See updated attachments: maintenance-sim-plan (rev B), runbook-checklist-v3.md

Diego
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-19T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SAFEGATE: simulation plan for private patch window, network gating & rollback

Quick shiproom update and post-sim notes (we executed the simulation at 09:30 PT):

- Execution: canary created (v2026-11-15-b-sim) at 09:40. NVA route and ingress drop rule applied to canary subnet at 09:48 (firewall ticket: ACME-CHG-1123).
- Observability: token-level cost spiked ~8% for 5 minutes during a forced cold start on canary; p95 latency exceeded 220ms for a 3-minute window at 09:53 — automated rollback trigger fired at 09:54 and sweep reverted to pinned baseline.
- Rollback: automated rollback completed at 09:55. No customer-facing errors observed because we kept canary traffic < 10% and used targeted ingress drops.
- Evidence collected: runbook snapshot, firewall ticket, DocuSign approval (signed during shiproom), telemetry export (s3://acme-evidence/2026-11-19/sim-1).

Attached: runbook-checklist-v3.md (with execution notes). Next steps: 1) tune cold-start mitigation for canaries 2) adjust automatic rollback thresholds to 180ms p95 for similar workloads 3) schedule a full-window simulated upgrade (non-sim) in low-risk lane.

—So
